Q: Is it normal for pattern matching to take forever when used on a 600kb+ string? A:

The main issue with the regex is .+ at the beginning of the regex.

When matching with a regex that starts with .+ this is what happens is:

  • start matching at the beginning of contents
  • capture from there to the end into .+ as it is greedy
  • check for match of the next token (literal " here, no match)
  • From the end, back-track one character at a time looking for a match
  • if there isn't a double quote in the string
    • advance one character from the beginning
    • capture from there the whole contents into .+
    • from the end back-track one character at a time ...

This easily leads to catastrophic backtracking on sufficiently long strings, but even without that result, it is immensely inefficient even on short strings. One can dive into the exact steps the regex provokes using an online regex tool such as regex101, it's especially useful to use the debugger and step through what's happening behind the scenes, but just looking at the number of steps can be illuminating (it scales exponentially with the length of contents)

Given what's asked in the question, the literal string "url":"/watch?v= is not present in contents and because the pattern starts with .+, string.find will figure that out slowly and exhaustively following the logic outlined above.

There are two obvious solutions for speeding up such a regex:

  • Anchor the pattern at the start with ^, as in "^.+\"url\":\"/watch%?v=.-\""
  • Remove .+ from the regex

Given the context in the question, the .+ isn't necessary and that's the safest/simplest solution.

Q: I am installing vscode in ubuntu linux....but I am getting this some unmet dependencies error A:

If you're baning your head against this because you're trying to install vscode on a linux VM running on a mac and when you run sudo snap install --classic code you get the message error: snap "code" is not available on stable for this architecture (arm64) but exists on other architectures (amd64)., then all you have to do is add the packages from microsoft so you can actually just install code from their sources:

wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor > microsoft.gpg
sudo install -o root -g root -m 644 microsoft.gpg /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/
sudo sh -c 'echo "deb [arch=arm64] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code stable main" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list'
sudo apt update

and then: sudo apt install code
